Request.Length > 0 before folding the request into the signed data. SIG(0) writes the request's octets and nothing else, so an empty request writes nothing under either reading. TSIGSigner's counterpart at line 337 looks identical and is not: it writes a two-octet length first, so an empty MAC puts 00 00 into the digest that a peer would not have.
